ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against PEP lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Spanish domestic criminal registry; advanced due diligence triggered where a UBO is a politically exposed person or linked to FATF high-risk jurisdictions; ongoing monitoring obligations under Articles 10 and 17 of Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online platform via the Colegio de Registradores de España e-Servicios system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: SL name must be in Spanish or another EU official language; if expressed in non-Roman characters, Spanish phonetic transliteration is mandatory. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name and must not imply official public authority status.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting public administration or regulated financial activity without prior ministerial approval
Offensive terms or terms contrary to Spanish public order
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (formerly DGRN) within one month from notification, attaching the negative certification application and legal arguments; alternatively the applicant may immediately submit a revised name application through the RMC portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered physical address in Spain is mandatory. Virtual office services are acceptable for an executive search and headhunting agency provided a physical establishment exists for official notices, records, and inspections; a pure post-office box without human presence does not satisfy Spanish commercial substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated <5% per operational year for this low-risk, non-regulated consultancy industry); however, unannounced labor authority and tax agency inspections may occur on a randomized basis.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (Articles 1-35)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de la Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital requirement of 3,000 EUR fully paid up at incorporation; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, as the sole shareholders and directors, unanimously resolve to incorporate the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada as follows: (1) Subscribe to the full share capital of 3,000 EUR; (2) Establish the registered office at a designated address in Madrid, Spain; (3) Appoint a Managing Director responsible for daily operations and a Corporate Secretary for compliance; (4) Authorize the immediate filing of the incorporation deed with the Registro Mercantil Central and all ancillary administrative procedures; (5) Open a corporate bank account and implement all necessary tax, social security, and AML compliance measures from the date of incorporation. This resolution complies fully with the Ley 1/2010 de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada and positions the company for seamless operational launch in the executive search sector.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary to draft the public deed of incorporation including share details, office, and bylaws. Submit shareholder IDs, draft documents, and address proof for notarization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incomplete submissions will be queried by the notary; resubmit corrected documents within 48 hours to proceed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed electronically via the official portal or in person at the provincial registry. Pay filing fees and obtain the registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If formal defects are noted, correct within 10 days or appeal to the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration certificate to Agencia Tributaria online portal to apply for NIF. Provide proof of address and bank details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is rejected, provide additional documentation or reapply after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Employment Agency Operating License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Empleo, Ministerio de Trabajo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit application with business plan, premises details, and security measures to the Ministry. Include environmental and safety clearances.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If incomplete, request additional information; appeal if denied after review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Official Spanish Tax Authority and Portal: https://www.aeat.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF automatically upon incorporation via Registro Mercantil. Non-resident foreign owners or branches require registration for NIF and tax residency determination; foreign entities with Spanish nexus file Form 036 with AEAT including corporate statutes, proof of activity, and Spanish tax representative appointment. VAT ID (NIF) issued post-approval within 30 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections available. Non-residents may elect specific regimes such as Simplified Tax Regime for SMEs (RETR) or opt for Spanish tax residency under Article 8 LIRPF. EU Anti-Hybrid Rules and CFC directives apply to mismatch structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 300,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for mandatory registration in general regime; lower thresholds apply for certain sectors or intra-EU supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Real-time Electronic Invoicing (SII - Sistema de Información Inmediata) with immediate transmission to AEAT, digital electronic stamping, API integration for large taxpayers, and mandatory issuance of factura electrónica for B2B and B2C supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported outside the EU or certain offshore services when destination is non-EU with proof of actual export and non-EU delivery; offshore services subject to specific territorial rules
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Despacho de Exportación), Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits trigger penalties of 75-100% of evaded VAT plus default interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rated treatment and any undue credits if export not substantiated or proceeds not repatriated within statutory timelines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting as the national competent monetary authority within the European System of Central Banks, with the Spanish Ministry of Economic Affairs and the General Directorate of International Trade and Investments (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones) exercising foreign investment and capital movement oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies the Eurozone capital and current account convertibility regime anchored in Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Capital movements, including share capital subscriptions, profit repatriation, dividends, retainer payments, and cross-border service settlements, are fully liberalised between Spain and other EU/EEA jurisdictions. No prior exchange control authorisation or central bank approval is required for current transactions or capital movements, although post-transaction statistical declaration obligations may apply for direct investment positions and certain financial operations. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders or foreign parent entities is unrestricted; a withholding tax and a debt-equity proportionality review may apply under corporate income tax thin-capitalisation provisions, but no currency convertibility or availability hurdle exists. For transactions involving non-resident counterparties in jurisdictions outside the EEA, the Spanish authorities retain scrutiny powers for sanctions, anti-money laundering (AML), and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) compliance, yet do not impose currency surrender or exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement and no statutory conversion ratio. Exporters are freely entitled to hold, transfer, convert, or retain proceeds in any currency within the limits of EU capital movement law. However, commercial invoicing, settlement, and related financial data must remain traceable and consistent with customs declarations and Bank of Spain balance-of-payments reporting thresholds. For transactions exceeding EUR 50,000, or when cross-border transfers trigger statistical reporting, Spanish residents must submit a 'Declaración de Movimientos de Pagos con el Exterior' (foreign payment transaction declaration) to the Bank of Spain through their financial institution. There is no requirement to convert export proceeds into euro; settlement may remain in any freely convertible currency, provided the underlying commercial documentation (export invoice, customs declaration, contract) meets the evidentiary standard of the reporting regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorised under the EU Electronic Money Directive (2009/110/EC) and passported into Spain are viable for low-complexity collection and disbursement flows, rated 'Medium-High' for the executive search and headhunting treasury profile. Legal constraints include the obligation to maintain safeguarding accounts at EU credit institutions, the absence of full deposit-guarantee coverage, and the requirement to ensure the EMI is registered with the Bank of Spain or within the European Economic Area passporting framework. With the stated target payment rail of 'Wise_B2B', Wise Europe SA (an authorised EMI) can operate in Spain under the Belgian passport; however, the entity should use Wise primarily for supplier settlements and small-ticket retainer collections, while keeping the primary treasury and capital account within a Tier 1 Spanish commercial bank to satisfy creditor comfort, tax audit traceability, and Bank of Spain statistical reporting. A fully offshore, non-EU EMI without an EEA passport is legally non-viable for serving a Spanish-resident corporate client on a continuous basis due to the Marketing of Financial Products and Services regime under MiFID II, the Spanish Securities Market Law, and AML Law 10/2010.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) with non-resident shareholders or directors, Spanish Tier 1 banks generally require at least one of the legal representatives or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact (apoderado) with sufficient powers to open accounts and execute treasury instructions to attend a physical or, increasingly, an advanced e-identification video KYC interview. Remote onboarding is permissible when the customer does not present elevated AML risk, when the shareholders are resident in a low-risk jurisdiction, and when the bank implements a certified customer identification process under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Directive (AMLD5/AMLD6) and Bank of Spain Circular 1/2022, but remote opening for the first account with a corporate vehicle commonly triggers a physical branch visit or a notarised power-of-attorney registration. As a defensive practice, the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) should be prepared to attend a physical meeting at the bank's Madrid or Barcelona corporate branch if the directors reside outside the EEA. The bank will require original or apostilled notarial documents; a Spanish-certified sworn translation is mandatory for any non-Spanish corporate document.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity — ultimate owners hidden behind a non-transparent holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A consolidated organisational chart, notarised and apostilled share register, certificate of ultimate beneficial owner issued by the corporate registry of each jurisdiction in the chain, resolutions appointing directors, and a written representation letter identifying every natural person owning more than 25% of the SL, together with passport copies and proof of residence and, if applicable, tax identification numbers (NIF/TIN). Prepare a Spanish sworn translation for each foreign registry excerpt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographical linkage — shareholders, beneficiaries, or counterparties located in sanctioned or FATF-high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated commercial contract and underlying executive-search engagement letters evidencing the legitimate business purpose; source-of-wealth declarations for the injecting capital; bank statements of the ultimate shareholder showing the lawful origin of funds; proof of export/import or service delivery and the commercial rationale for any cross-border wire; and a legal opinion from a qualified counsel confirming no conflict with EU/UN/OFAC sanctions regimes. Where a Latin American shareholder chain is present, include a NOM-151 or comparable jurisdictional stamp, and complete the enhanced due diligence questionnaire provided by the Spanish bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or mismatched economic profile — newly formed SL with low share capital (EUR 3,000) and immediately receiving abroad-sourced retainer revenue exceeding the capital base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company's business plan, projected cash flows, executed headhunting agreements with corporate clients, invoices and service contracts demonstrating actual economic activity, the ES_SL's corporate income tax and VAT pre-registration, and the professional credentials of the directors. Include a notarised board resolution that identifies the bank account as the sole treasury account and confirms that future cash flows will be exclusively from executive-search services. Provide references, LinkedIn or professional biographies of the management, and the current annual accounts if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire purpose inconsistency — payment references indicating consultancy or general services that conflict with ISIC 7830 executive-search scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardised payment descriptions embedding the invoice number, the contractual scope, and an explicit reference to 'executive search and headhunting under ISIC 7830'. Prepare a purpose-code mapping table and retain the supporting contract, retainer letter, candidate placement evidence, and final placement report. Ensure the Bank of Spain foreign-transaction declaration code matches the service classification (payment for professional services — 'Servicios de búsqueda de ejecutivos' under the EBOPS/BPM6 standard) and that the cumulative inbound and outbound flows reconcile with invoices and tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political Exposed Persons (PEP) indicators in the directorship or ownership of the SL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed PEP self-declaration, the CVs and public-office records of all directors and shareholders where relevant, the ultimate source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, confirmation of economic activity in a commercial context unrelated to political influence, and a legal risk assessment from the bank-appointed compliance unit. Where a PEP is identified, secure a written reference from a reputable financial institution in the PEP's country of residence and, if necessary, a senior management approval file per the bank's risk appetite.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection into the SL follows the EU liberalised capital-movement regime. The sole/foreign shareholder wires the subscribed or contributed capital through the SWIFT network using an MT103 message or, for euro-denominated transfers from within the SEPA zone, an SEPA Credit Transfer. The beneficiary bank must receive the transfer with a clear purpose code aligned to Spanish balance-of-payments nomenclature: use category 'Direct investment — Equity capital' ('Inversión directa — Capital social') and include the reference 'STA' (sociedad de actividad extranjera) or 'NF' where required. The SL's statutory share capital may be set at or above the minimum of EUR 3,000; no escrow account is legally required, but for a cross-border investor using a Capital Escrow Account, the funds must be held in a segregated account opened for the company in formation until the notary executes the public deed. Recommended transfer instructions include a letter from the investor to the ordering bank with: the SL's name, NIF (tax ID), CIF/statistical code, the commercial invoice or capital injection agreement if applicable, the exact amount, and a narrative description 'Equity contribution for ES_SL — ISIC 7830 executive search activities'. The receiving bank should be supplied with the notarial deed and the Bank of Spain file for foreign investment (if the stake reaches the 10% threshold for direct-investment statistical purposes). For a contribution of services or IP in lieu of cash, a sworn valuation and registration with the Spanish Mercantile Registry is mandatory before the bank books the asset as capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for a cross-border executive-search agency settle primarily through: (a) international SWIFT MT103 transfers for non-SEPA destination banks; (b) SEPA Credit Transfers for euro payments within the EEA; and (c) commercial letters of credit (documentary credits) only when the executive-search contract imposes milestone-based escrow, candidate signing bonus protection, or split-fee structures with international corporates — although standard headhunting retainer fees rarely require a full LC. For trade settlements to Latin-American beneficiaries, use correspondent banking channels with the Spanish bank's London, Miami, or Lima branches to guarantee final delivery of funds; include the invoice number, a precise purpose code for business services, and, where the destination requires an SWIFT coverage message, instruct the cover through 'COV' or use the bank's e-banking template for commercial payments. For high-value retainer fees exceeding EUR 10,000, the bank may request the underlying fee agreement and an updated certificate of the SL's tax compliance. The payment rails should be supported by a treasury policy that separates operational disbursements (salaries, candidate bonuses, contractor fees) from client settlement accounts, and includes a dual-authorisation matrix for senior directors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards / outright forwards) for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/LatAm currency conversions, with maturities matching the executive-search retainer and placement-fee cash-flow cycle.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid Latin American currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, certain local currencies) to hedge translation and settlement exposure embedded in cross-border retainer receipts or candidate sign-on bonuses without requiring physical delivery of the non-convertible currency.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and interest-rate swaps in combination) when the SL maintains term bank debt or prepares to bid on large multi-year executive-search mandates with fixed monthly retainer inflows from a multinational client, to concurrently hedge interest-rate and currency risk.

Over-the-counter (OTC) derivative transactions are restricted to execution through licensed Spanish credit institutions or EU investment firms and must be disclosed to the Bank of Spain for statistical surveillance; no speculative or leveraged hedges are permitted without an adequate risk-management board resolution and, where applicable, the EMIR clearing obligation threshold.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential rates for qualifying small entities: 15% on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base for newly created entities in the first two profitable years (Art. 29.1 LIS); reduced 15%/20% history for entities with turnover under EUR 10 million; for tax periods beginning on/after 1 January 2024, micro-entities with net turnover below EUR 1 million benefit from 17% on the first EUR 50,000 of taxable base and 20% on the remainder under RDL 4/2024. Structural incentives include the capitalization reserve (10% reduction of taxable base), small-entity leveling reserve (Art. 105 LIS), R&D&I tax credits (25% of R&D expenses, 12% of technological innovation expenses, Arts. 31-35 LIS), and the participation exemption on dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS) subject to minimum holding and substance conditions.
